title: Default auto_accept threshold (0.8) is structurally unreachable for model_initiated + filesystem evidence
body:
Compute the ceiling before assuming a threshold is reachable: cappedConfidence = RELIABILITY_CAP[provenance] * CAPTURE_ORIGIN_FACTOR[capture_origin]. For the most common autonomous case (capture_origin: model_initiated, best verified evidence: filesystem), the ceiling is 0.85 * 0.9 = 0.765, which is below the default auto_accept.confidence_threshold of 0.8. That default therefore only ever admits capture_origin: user_explicit proposals (0.85*1=0.85) or ones carrying an observed user_correction artifact (0.855-0.95) -- never a model's own filesystem-evidenced finding. Don't diagnose this as a bug in the proposal or in sweepAutoAccept; it's the reliability ladder in src/engine/reliability.js working as designed. Flag it as a product decision (intentional gate vs. needs recalibration) rather than silently reproposing with different evidence to force a pass.

Why: Verified live on 2026-09-19: proposed a genuinely well-evidenced lesson (dd/store/legacy-home-dirs-verified-and-purged) with a filesystem-verified evidence_ref and capture_origin model_initiated. It computed to confidence 0.765 and stayed lifecycle_state candidate after a listing fetch (which runs sweepAutoAccept per commit f8bc4de) with auto_accept enabled and threshold 0.8. Confirmed the 0.765 ceiling algebraically from RELIABILITY_CAP.filesystem=0.85 and CAPTURE_ORIGIN_FACTOR.model_initiated=0.9 in src/engine/reliability.js.

evidence.summary: sweepAutoAccept computes projectedConfidence via cappedConfidence and skips admission when projectedConfidence < config.auto_accept.confidence_threshold

v1.trigger: When evaluating or tuning auto_accept.confidence_threshold, or explaining why a well-evidenced model-proposed candidate never auto-admits
